I was somewhat enjoying this game as a side-scrolling beat'em up, but as I got further in, the flaws eventually caught up to it. To begin with, the game is fairly good - the simple combo system allows you to do fairly long juggle chains (almost infinite if timed correctly). The graphics are nice, and the tilted 2.5D design and art style is pretty cool. 

The problem lies in the overall UX design being poor. There's no way to change your alt character once you've made the choice in the campaign, so you can't experiment and change your mind. Can't seem to do chapter select, so you gotta play through it from the start. 

What got me completely off the game was the level 5-2 with the 3 knife throwing enemies that release the frogs. It's absolutely ridiculous how many exploding frogs they release - and while you can double-jump and air dash to avoid them, the 3 enemies just dash to the other side, throw some knives and again begin releasing frogs. My alt character is the rapper, and he does have a really slow move that can hit the frogs from range, but you get knifed in the face fairly quickly, followed by an endless stun lock with frog stream. Just very poorly thought out - fairly unplayable single player.

I Am The Hero looks pretty and has no plot substance. The main character is a boring nobody who is fighting other nobodies for no clear reason. The art is pretty, and the 2.5D perspective is interesting, but there's not a witty line or interesting character hiding anywhere.

Gameplay is focused on combos gathered from juggling and bouncing opponents all over the screen. Your opponents will never stop trying to hit you, and will even pile-on when you do get hit. There is no good defensive option. All of your default attacks have horrible range. So, you'll always be trying to track the last opponent that you sent bouncing everywhere in order to follow up on your combo while also attempting to avoid hits from just out of your range. If it's all too hard, too bad, there's no easy mode.

I Am The Hero demands precision without rewarding any effort you make with any interesting content. Most beat'em ups have the decency to at least give you usable normals as a way to ease you into the challenge. Waste of time.

Графон отличный, музон драйвовый (но раздражает, если надолго застрял на одном уровне), боёвка хорошая. Прям видно, как авторы вдохновлялись BattleToads - что по выпученным глазам врагов, что по структуре уровней (1-1,2-1,2-2...), что по доминанткам, аккуратно скопированным из источника.

Особенно порадовал угол камеры для 2D-игры - настолько простая идея, НИГДЕ ранее мне не встречавшаяся. Она ведь даже не стала 2.5D от этого, потому что спрайты остались спрайтами, но ведь всё равно так кажется! Изумительно.

После обычного прохождения решил поднять планку сложности, но быстро отвалился. Что на последних уровнях, что на повышенной difficulty, враги тупо жирнее, [b]игнорируют[/b] стан (а это критично) и аптечки почти не сыпятся. Кстати, ты прям чувствуешь, что после поражения игра "подкручивает" вероятность выпадения бонусов, поэтому можно первую попытку не напрягаться, а просто опиздюлиться, чтобы после этого уже хоть как-то пройти последние локации.

Конечно, очень многое зависит от комбы, но я так и не смог сделать больше сотни, потому что не получилось [b]прочувствовать[/b] удачные связки. Вот ты подбрасываешь врага, вот ты пытаешься до него достать - и перелетаешь, а он падает вниз, встаёт и хреначит по тебе, сбивая комбо. И это только один пример из кучи. Особенно мерзко выходит с боссами в конце: они тупо врубают свою ульту, и шансов не получить ни единого удара попросту нет, хоть ты обтыкай RT.

Короче, тут явно нужно играть вдвоём. Онлайн - сами понимаете, какой: игра не так уж известна, поэтому людей в Сети нет.
А если соло - пройти на обычной сложности, смачно харкнуть и забить, пока не притащишь к телеку товарища. Ну и режим "онлайн"-челленджей (читай: оффлайн драка с таблицей рекордов [i]времени[/i], буэээ) - та ещё дрочка, тоже ну её нахрен.

А может, потому что на геймпаде запретили D-Pad + нельзя увернуться двойным нажатием, только RT. Короче, всё равно я делаю не самый лучший вывод.

After that it just reached a point where the game was more about keeping my character juggled than allowing me to play. I could dodge but as soon as the dodge animation ended, I was hit again. It’s primarily because of the mechanics of the enemies, certain enemies in small clusters or even on their own can go toe to toe with you but when you start filling the screen with them it results in an absolute mess that makes me wonder if the game had any QA. Multiple enemies that vomit, throw projectiles, vanish into clothing, drop explosives that stun you etc… all of this happening at the same time, doesn’t really give you any room to actually play.

Overall, it WAS a great game up until that point but it deteriorated really quickly, so unfortunately I can’t really recommend it cause you’ll be wasting your money (I luckily only dropped just under $5AU on sale) and now I can’t really finish it and even if I could, I don’t really care to after seeing this. A very great game that I would recommend except for a few gameplay elements that sour the experience.

First, the game has okay controls for a beat 'em up. The graphics and music serve the game well. Enemy and level design carry a lot of character and polish. The game has a solid foundation upon which a legendary beat 'em up could exist.

Unfortunately, there's a number of design decisions that, when combined, make for questionable gameplay. First, the player can only move left and right along a single fixed plane instead of also being able to move up and down such as in games like Castle Crashers and Final Fight. This isn't a big deal on its own, but it does pose a problem when there's a large number of enemies, slow-moving or static hazards, and projectiles on the screen. Gameplay devolves into a whole lot of jumping and not a whole lot of fighting when this occurs. This is just not fun. I didn't want bad 2D platformer gameplay.

This becomes a bigger problem in the later levels as it seems this game's idea of a challenge is just filling the screen with enemies. Even dodging isn't an option as you get hit as soon as your invincibilty frames end as there is almost certainly something occupying the same space as your character (enemy, projectile, bomb, etc.).

These situations feel like they arise a bit too often, and that's likely due to how little damage your character does. I'm sure this is meant to enable some high-hit combos, but it instead sets the stage for some very stale gameplay as there are only so many ways to launch an enemy into the air, jump up to them, combo, and repeat. This effectively becomes the strongest tool in your arsenal as few enemies are capable of hitting you out of the air.

This means gameplay devolves into finding a safe place to stand long enough to launch as many enemies as you can into the air and juggle them there for as long as possible. And this isn't necessarily a bad thing as it's a valid tactic in a lot of beat 'em ups, but here the game just doesn't allow for much variety within or outside of this technique. WIth it, you launch, combo, launch, combo, etc. for as long as you can, and you're really only mixing up the kicks and punches. Big whoop. Without it, your best hope is timing a punch when the opponent attacks to get an instant and powerful counterattack called a 'critical'. This move is where the character feels the strongest, but again, gameplay devolves when many characters get on the screen as there's seemingly no clean way to counter so much or easily get back into position without playing the jumping platformer games I mentioned earlier.

Here's a list of other random annoyances:

Buttons in the hero guide show keys even if you use controls. Some buttons are correct if you remapped, some aren't. The instant-death elevator stage.

Enemies taking cover outside of the screen.

Undocumented cooldowns on EX moves (can't seem to do the same back-to-back even if you have meter?)

Your character can get hit on the ground, but can't get up to avoid it unless you have meter.

Long unnecessary EX moves that continue to wiff their overly long and unnecesssary animation whose hitbox can't seem to miss or juggle the enemy away more than half the time.

The boss on 6-3 is nothing but a horribly unfun fight. Can anything he does be critical countered? Who knows? It seems you just have to use an ungodly amount of cheese to nickel-and-dime his health down.

Save your money. This game has a solid premise that is ruined by some really bad game design decisions. The few hours you spend with it will be bittersweet at best.
